DATA NOTE: The July 11 bundle was unavailable at pull time after five retry attempts. This brief uses July 7 lake sections as the data baseline, augmented by the July 11 Ukraine Theater ingest (131 new items), live supplementary feeds (GDACS, USGS, EONET), and up to 12 web research pulls reflecting conditions as of July 11 UTC.

Headline

Three interlocking arcs dominate this morning. Russia's refinery attrition campaign crossed a domestic threshold this week: fuel shortages now affect 83 of Russia's 89 regions and 50 million people, Putin's VTsIOM approval has fallen to 66% (its sharpest weekly drop since 2022), and Urals crude at $41.66/bbl runs $17.34 below Moscow's $59 budget breakeven with no near-term recovery path visible. The NATO Ankara summit closed with a 70 billion euro Ukraine support pledge and a US license for Ukraine to domestically manufacture Patriot interceptors, while Trump expressed optimism about a settlement "on the horizon" -- two signals pointing in the same direction only if Moscow is also moving toward talks, for which the evidence remains thin. France produced a major political inflection: an appeals court upheld Marine Le Pen's embezzlement conviction but shortened her electoral ban to 15 months, theoretically reopening her path to the 2027 presidential ballot. Watch areas fired: Russia oil sanctions perimeter (25 items, threshold 5), US tariff and trade dockets (17 items, threshold 3), Israel-Iran-Hezbollah axis (15 items, Macron Damascus explosions, Bahrain), and Central bank divergence (JPY at 162.1, +2.3 sigma above 90-day mean).

Macro Situation

The Treasury curve is modestly positive: the 10y-2y spread at +35 basis pointsfred.stlouisfed.org, with the 10-year at 4.49% (DGS10fred.stlouisfed.org), the 2-year at 4.14% (DGS2fred.stlouisfed.org), and the 30-year approaching 5.0% at 4.98% (DGS30fred.stlouisfed.org). Fed Funds effective at 3.63% (DFFfred.stlouisfed.org) and SOFR tracking exactly (SOFRfred.stlouisfed.org). Against July 2025, the front end has fallen sharply (2Y was ~4.92%), while the long end has barely moved; the net effect is de-inversion. The 30-year approaching 5% is the principal fiscal signal: it reflects long-term supply risk, not imminent rate action [medium].

Two variables exceed 2 sigma above the 90-day window. JPY/USD at 162.1 (markets_global, July 7) is approximately +2.3 sigma. The Bank of Japan raised rates and spent over $73 billion on intervention since June without closing the 325-bp differential to the US. A sustained break above 162 tests whether Tokyo can defend further without triggering a formal G7 coordination discussion. Bitcoin futures (BITO) at +3.60% and approximately +2.8 sigma on the 90-day window track the broader crypto risk-on cycle. Neither signal is independently catastrophic, but the JPY move is structurally important: every 10-yen weakening adds roughly 0.3% to Japanese import-price inflation, compounding BOJ's dilemma [high].

Core PCE stands at 130.082 (PCEPILFEfred.stlouisfed.org) as of May. Headline CPI at 333.979 (CPIAUCSLfred.stlouisfed.org) and core CPI at 336.121 (CPILFESLfred.stlouisfed.org). June unemployment held at 4.2% (UNRATEfred.stlouisfed.org) with 158.98 million nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMSfred.stlouisfed.org). JOLTS job openings at 7.594 million as of May (JTSJOLfred.stlouisfed.org) remain elevated but declining. The labor market is softening without contraction; the Fed's July 29 meeting is universally priced as a hold (Polymarket: 0% for 50+ bp hikepolymarket.com).

EUR/USD at 1.1448 (DEXUSEUfred.stlouisfed.org) -- the euro has gained roughly 6% against the dollar since early April on a combination of European defense spending momentum and dollar softening. CNY/USD at 6.7886 (DEXCHUSfred.stlouisfed.org) is stable. The Fed balance sheet at $6.72 trillionfred.stlouisfed.org and M2 at $23.05 trillion (M2SLfred.stlouisfed.org) show no acute tightening signal. VIX at 15.81 (VIXCLSfred.stlouisfed.org) suggests no near-term equity stress despite the geopolitical noise, which itself is a mild complacency indicator [low].

WTI at $71.87 (DCOILWTICOfred.stlouisfed.org) reflects post-Hormuz-reopening normalization after April's $116 peak. The more operationally significant figure is Urals at $41.66 -- the gap to Russia's $59 budget breakeven is now locked in for the July quarter, implying a fiscal deficit on the energy account alone of approximately $5.3 billion per month at current production levels [high].

Markets

The July 6 session printed broad risk appetite: SPY +0.87% to 751.28finance.yahoo.com, QQQ +1.43% to 722.82finance.yahoo.com, and MSCI EM (EEM) +2.85% to 67.57finance.yahoo.com -- the EM outperformance relative to large-cap US is a soft dollar rotation. Russell 2000 (IWM) lagged at +0.44%, indicating risk concentration in mega-cap tech rather than the domestic small-cap complex, consistent with the AI capex cycle pricing pattern [medium].

Samsung posted record Q2 operating profit at ₩89.4 trillion ($58.4B)english.hani.co.kr, 19x year-over-year on HBM3/AI GPU memory demand. Revenue exceeded ₩171 trillion, more than double Q2 2025. The stock sold off 7%: markets are reading the earnings as a margin peak signal, with the 10.5% semiconductor-profit wage provision and capex intensity implying compressed returns on the next investment cycle. If the market's negative read on record Samsung earnings is correct, it leads the broader AI infrastructure supply chain by 6-9 months [medium].

Gold (GLD) +1.06% to $382.13 and Agriculture (DBA) +2.99% to $27.54 were notable commodity movers. The agriculture move is worth flagging in the context of Russia's fuel crisis: Krasnodar harvest logistics are being disrupted by the regional gasoline shortage, with additional fuel costs for Russian farmers potentially reaching ₽14 billion ($184M) this summer. Natural gas (UNG) +1.12%. Credit spreads compressed: HYG (high yield) +0.20%, LQD (investment grade) +0.03%. VXX fell 2.50% -- markets are covering volatility hedges into a geopolitically noisy weekend, which historically precedes complacency inflection points [low].

The broader dollar picture from markets_global (July 7): USD/EUR at 0.875 (EUR strong), USD/JPY at 162.13 (yen near weakest in 30+ years), USD/GBP at 0.748, USD/CHF at 0.806. The simultaneity of euro strength and yen weakness while the dollar index drifts lower is unusual: it reflects European exceptionalism on defense spending while Japan remains caught in the rate differential trap.

Regional Briefings

North America

The dominant domestic policy arc is deregulatory rulemaking velocity. The July 7 Federal Register produced 17 new items in a single day across energy, labor, environment, civil rights, and aviation -- a high-water mark for this quarter. The HHS NCI Cancer Education Program rescission proposalfederalregister.gov is one of the smaller but symbolically notable items: a grant program that has operated for decades is being removed from the Code of Federal Regulations, not reformed.

In campaign finance, the Maine Senate vacancywashingtonpost.com created by Platner's suspension reshapes the Senate map. Maine Democrats must select a nominee by July 27. The seat that was considered safely Democratic is now competitive. Cory Booker (NJ)fec.gov at $32.27M raised maintains his position as the best-funded Northern incumbent running for re-election.

Canada's submarine procurement decision has geopolitical downstream effects: South Korea's DAPA confirmed Canada selected Germany over South Koreaworld.kbs.co.kr for its submarine project, citing NATO alliance considerations. The decision signals that security alignment factors -- not just industrial or cost criteria -- increasingly govern NATO-bloc defense procurement, a pattern that will constrain future South Korean defense export pitches to alliance members.

South America

The Polymarket Colombia World Cup marketpolymarket.com sits at 3% to win, consistent with their position as a quarterfinal-or-better threat but not a tournament favorite. Argentina (18%) faces Egypt in the bracket, with their advance priced at 86% on Polymarket's specific match marketpolymarket.com. The 2026 FIFA World Cup, hosted across the US, Mexico, and Canada, is generating the most liquid Polymarket sports books in the platform's history, with aggregate 24h volume exceeding $50M.

No high-severity conflict or political events from South America in the July 7 data. The Presidential Determination on Venezuelafederalregister.gov is the most consequential open thread; its interaction with PDVSA oil export sanctions and Maduro's political position warrants monitoring into the August OPEC meeting cycle.

Regional economic conditions remain mixed. Argentina's Milei government continues its fiscal consolidation program. Brazil's Lula-era commodity export cycle is supporting primary surplus targets. Chile's lithium royalty reform remains a moving variable for the Critical Minerals watch area.

Europe

The Marine Le Pen appeals court rulingfrance24.com is the European political headline of the week. The court upheld her EU funds embezzlement conviction but reduced the electoral ban from five years to 15 months. With the 2027 French presidential election scheduled for April, the 15-month ban from July 7 ends in approximately October 2027 -- leaving ambiguity about whether she is eligible. Le Pen previously stated she would not run if convicted; she has not issued a definitive new statement. Jordan Bardella, her designated successor within Rassemblement National, remains the fallback candidate. The 2027 race is now genuinely three-way among Bardella/Le Pen (RN), Macron's centrist bloc, and the fragmented left.

Spain reached the FIFA World Cup semifinals, defeating Portugal 1-0 in injury time through Mikel Merino. Cristiano Ronaldo confirmed his retirement from international footballfrance24.com following the defeat, closing a 21-year Portugal career. Belgium knocked out the United States teamfrance24.com in a match marked by red card controversy; Belgium advances to face Spain, while France (33% Polymarket favorite) and Argentina (18%) contest the other semifinal path.

Germany's Bundeswehr is now one of the country's most attractive employers for young peoplefrance24.com, with applications rising 23% in January amid an economic recession and large-scale industrial job cuts. The report notes students are treating military service as a "Plan B" as private-sector opportunities contract. This is a structural rearmament signal independent of government policy targets [high].

Russia and Post-Soviet

Putin's approval trajectory is deteriorating. VTsIOM (state pollster) recorded approval at 66.0%meduza.io, down from 66.9% the prior week -- the sharpest consecutive weekly decline since the 2022 invasion. The independent Levada Center put approval at 74% in Junethemoscowtimes.com, down from 79% in May. The causal link is direct: 20% of VTsIOM respondents named the gasoline shortage as the week's defining event. The fall matters precisely because both polling institutions show the same direction simultaneously, which under Russia's historically high approval-stabilization tends to indicate a genuine shift rather than noise [high].

Alert

The Novosibirsk Tolmachevo airport flight restrictions (July 6, cited in Ukraine theater section) add to the cascade: this is Russia's largest Siberian hub and the primary transit airport for much of Siberia. Restrictions of the type reported (typically issued when a region declares "heightened alert") suggest the fuel crisis has reached logistical chokepoints beyond road networks. The ISW July 10 assessment confirms: "Russia's oil refining industry is failing to meet rising domestic gasoline demand as the Ukrainian long-range strike campaign continues to degrade refining capacity."

The Kremlin suspected shadow fleet drone campaign over Europearstechnica.com -- Russian intelligence reportedly using shadow tankers as drone launch platforms -- is the sharpest single escalation signal outside Ukraine theater. It transforms the sanctions enforcement debate from a purely economic contest into a security one. If confirmed at the operational level, it will accelerate the flag-clampdown that is already forcing Chinese and UAE operators to retreat from the fleet.

Middle East

The Damascus IED attack near Macron's hotelnbcnews.com on July 7 wounded 18 people. Macron was in transit when the devices detonated -- one hidden in a garbage bin, one in a parked car on convoy routes. No group claimed responsibility. The devices' placement on vehicle egress routes, combined with the absence of a claim, points toward professional intelligence-service tradecraft rather than opportunistic terrorism; the intended message was disruption of the visit, not mass casualties [medium]. Macron continued his visit and met with Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa -- making him the first EU head of state to visit Syria since Assad's fall. The France-Syria rehabilitation track is proceeding despite the attack signal.

The Bahrain Fifth Fleet headquartersmilitary.com complex at Juffair has been subject to a sustained Iranian drone and missile campaign since February 28 (initial major strike: one killed, two injured, $400M damage). The July 10 fire report in the Ukraine theater section likely reflects continuation of this campaign rather than a discrete new escalation; no independently sourced confirmation of a July 11 attack is available at brief time.

Qatar's FM demand that Iran "cease any practices that threaten regional security and endanger maritime and energy security" is new public pressure from a Gulf state that has historically maintained covert working relationships with Tehran. The combination of Qatar's statement and Iran's parliament speaker accusing the US of violating an MoU suggests the Gulf-Iran diplomatic working framework is under acute stress [medium].

Mahmoud Abbas leadership transition: Polymarket's Abbas departure before 2027 marketpolymarket.com is priced at effectively 0% on $2.4M of 24h volume. The paradox -- high volume on a near-zero-priced outcome -- suggests either liquidity provision activity or an options-style hedge on low-probability PA instability. Abbas's continued tenure is the base case; the volume implies the market is actively pricing the tail.

Lebanon: Israeli bombing continues in Beit Yahoun in Nabatiyeh Governorateliveuamap.com, with Israeli Army demolition operations inside Khiam ongoing. The pattern is consistent with the continuing post-ceasefire infrastructure clearance operations in southern Lebanon.

East Asia

Samsung's Q2 2026 earningsenglish.hani.co.kr are the macro signal of the week for East Asia. The ₩89.4 trillion operating profit on ₩171 trillion revenue, driven by HBM3 memory for AI accelerators, confirms South Korea's position as the primary beneficiary of the global AI infrastructure buildout. The negative market reaction (stock -7%) reflects concerns that: (a) HBM3 margin expansion has peaked as TSMC and DRAM competitors ramp capacity, and (b) Samsung's 10.5% semiconductor-profit wage provision implies compressed free cash flow through 2026. The parallel Canadian submarine decision rejecting South Korea in favor of Germany adds a defense-procurement setback to the week's picture.

The China-aligned Roundcube exploitation campaignthehackernews.com against physics and engineering departments of US and Canadian universities is the week's sharpest cyber-espionage signal. Roundcube webmail flaws targeting university physics/engineering departments is a well-precedented STEM talent intelligence collection vector; the same playbook was used in the earlier BRONZE SILHOUETTE campaigns. The universities targeted were not named in available reporting.

Tenda router firmware with undocumented authentication backdoors (CERT/CC warningthehackernews.com) is the week's supply-chain hardware signal. Tenda manufactures low-cost routers widely deployed in small-office and home environments; an authentication backdoor in firmware affects potentially millions of devices globally.

The Bangladesh flood alertgdacs.org (GDACS Green, July 9-11) and Guatemala flood (GDACS Green, July 9-11) are the week's active humanitarian flooding events. Bangladesh flooding during the pre-monsoon window, when river channels are not yet fully loaded, typically indicates extreme rainfall in the upstream Brahmaputra-Meghna system; downstream Dhaka and Sylhet flooding risk will escalate through August if the pattern persists.

No high-severity conflict items for South Asia from the July 7 data. India's Mukesh Ambani ($89.52B, #22 Forbes) and Gautam Adani ($89.01B, #24) remain proximate on the wealth ranking, a function of divergent infrastructure versus telecom/retail trajectories.

World Leaders -- Speaking and Moving

Trump attended the NATO Ankara summit (July 7-9) and held bilaterals with both Zelensky and Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa. Trump's statements on Ukraine were notably positive -- "I think we're getting much closer than people realize" and "President Putin wants it to end" -- and he separately approved a US license for Ukraine to domestically manufacture Patriot air defense systemsabcnews.com, the most concrete military-industrial commitment of the summit. Trump stated from Ankara: "I hope to end Ukraine war soon." He also threatened Iran and Spain during the summit but closed calling it "unity."

Zelensky signed new drone supply agreements with Estonia, Netherlands, and Denmark at the Ankara summit. He stated Ukrainian forces are eliminating approximately 30,000 Russian troops per month. His framing of the peace situation was more cautious than Trump's; Zelensky's acceptance of negotiation language is hedged with his standard conditions (sovereignty, reparations, security guarantees).

Macron visited Syria on July 7 in a landmark first EU-leader visit to post-Assad Syriafrance24.com, meeting Ahmed al-Sharaa as part of France's Syria rehabilitation diplomacy. The Damascus IED attackaljazeera.com near his hotel (18 wounded; Macron was in transit and uninjured) did not terminate the visit. The Elysee confirmed Macron safe. Macron had also been at the NATO Ankara summit the same week, making it a high-exposure diplomatic cycle.

Marine Le Pen faces a 15-month ban from public office after the appeals court ruling (July 7). She has not made a public statement on whether she will attempt to run in the 2027 presidential election.

Wikidata leader-roster changes: Zero succession or death events flagged for the July 7 window.

Ahmed al-Sharaa (Syria's new president) received Macron and separately agreed to meet Trump on the final day of the NATO summit. Both major-power meetings in the same week signal Syria's accelerated reintegration into the international system.

Cyber and Biosecurity

The most significant cyber items from the July 7 BleepingComputer/Hacker News feeds:

Januscape: A 16-year-old Linux kernel vulnerabilitybleepingcomputer.com allowing VM escape and arbitrary code execution on Intel and AMD hosts. A 16-year window means the vulnerability likely exists in nearly all production Linux deployments. VM escape capabilities are cloud-platform tier risks; the combination of Intel and AMD coverage means this is not architecture-specific. Patch cadence will be the key variable: hyperscaler deployment of patches takes days; enterprise on-premises deployments can take weeks to months [high].

BeyondTrust critical authentication bypass: Two critical flaws in Remote Support and Privileged Remote Accessbleepingcomputer.com allow unauthenticated attackers to take control of devices. BeyondTrust is widely used in enterprise privileged access management; authentication bypass in PAM software is approximately the highest-severity credential-chain vulnerability category. Patch immediately [high].

China-aligned Roundcube exploitation against US/Canadian university physics/engineering departments is an academic STEM intelligence collection campaign consistent with BRONZE SILHOUETTE and similar clustersthehackernews.com.

Tenda router backdoor: Undocumented authentication backdoorthehackernews.com in multiple Tenda firmware versions. CERT/CC advisory in force. Tenda devices are prevalent in cost-sensitive SME and home environments globally.

The CISA KEV catalog shows no new additions in the July 7 window (8 active CVEs, most recent added July 1). The CVE-2026-45659 Microsoft SharePoint Server deserialization flaw (remediation deadline July 4) and CVE-2026-48558 SimpleHelp authentication bypass (deadline July 2) are past their required federal remediation dates and remain the highest-priority exposure for any government-connected network not yet patched.

Weak Signals -- Small Things That May Matter

Cross-section data (cross_section.json) is unavailable for July 11; the most recent available is July 7. The highest-confidence cross-section recurrences identifiable from manual review this cycle:

Russia energy-fiscal stress appears simultaneously in GDELT GKG (sanction perimeter articles), macro (Urals at $42, FRED series), markets (WTI vs. Urals chart, energy commodity moves), billionaires (Urals pricing context), Ukraine theater (ISW refinery assessment), and commentary (Hankyoreh editorial). The convergence across six sections is the brief's highest-confidence weak signal: Russia's oil revenues are collapsing, its domestic fuel supply is fracturing, its political approval is declining, and the shadow fleet architecture that partially protected the revenue base is contracting as Chinese and UAE operators pull back. No single section reveals this magnitude of systemic stress; the multi-section view does [high].

French political restructuring appears in foreign news (Le Pen appeals court ruling), Ukraine theater (Macron Damascus visit), GDELT regions/GKG (World Cup / Le Pen / Syria), and VIP flights (French medical/SAMU aircraft operating in normal patterns, no emergency dispersal). The Le Pen 15-month electoral ban is the smallest element of the French political week but potentially the most consequential at 18 months' range: it transforms the 2027 election from a known outcome (RN without its founder) to an open one [medium].

Januscape + BeyondTrust auth bypass appearing in the same week as the China-aligned Roundcube university campaign and the Tenda firmware backdoor represents unusual clustering of high-severity foundational infrastructure vulnerabilities. VM escape, PAM authentication bypass, academic webmail exploitation, and hardware backdoor are four different attack-surface categories; their temporal clustering may be coincidental or may reflect coordinated adversarial pressure on the period between scheduled patch cycles [low].

Three additional weak signals:

The Belgian Air Component flight dispersalopensky-network.org across six European and Mediterranean positions simultaneously is unusual for a 50-aircraft air force. The most proximate explanation is a NATO interoperability exercise concurrent with the Ankara summit; a secondary explanation is forward pre-positioning for a contingency. The Egypt position (JAF1KW) is the outlier: a Belgian F-16 transiting near Cairo aligns with no immediately obvious NATO exercise [low].

The woman suspected in the Monaco bombing found shot dead near Kyivfrance24.com suggests a GUR counter-proliferation or source-protection operation inside Ukraine. The Monaco attack's targeting logic remains unclear; the killing of the suspected perpetrator before interrogation closes that line of inquiry and opens a new one about what she knew and who ordered her killed [medium].

The Graham Platner Polymarket move (+87 percentage points on dropping out of the Maine primary, cited in Marginal Revolution's decision-markets post) is structurally interesting: $16.31M raised and disbursed with only $2.18M on hand means the campaign had committed nearly all its resources before the suspension. This is a campaign-finance structure consistent with a candidate who had polling confidence right up to the scandal breaking [medium].
